To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genus g free energies F g (g≥1) of matrix models satisfy the holomorphic anomalies equations (HAEs) of Bershadsky et al., that these HAEs are satisfied as well by the genus g free energy F g (g ≥ 1) of the open sector of the matrix models, and that the genus g open string free energies F g,open (g≥1), defined as the sum of the free energies of the matrix model and the open sector, satisfy

(1) The genus g free energy of matrix models is a modular invariant, nonholomorphic function of the classical spectral parameters, and (2) these nonholomorphic functions satisfy the holomorphic anomalous equations of Bershadskii, Cecotti, Oguri and Vafa (BCOV).

the genus $g$ free energies of matrix model can be promoted to non-holomorphic modular invariant amplitudes which satisfy the holomorphic anomoly equations of Bershadskii, Cecotti, Vafa and Ooguri, and the holomorphic anomoy equations for the open sector of matrix model are derived.
